subject: project.new's precondition, and what it means for the destructive half of the qualification program
question: 32 of the deferred operations are destructive and belong to a Phase C-live with a disposable fixture. Can that fixture be created from a running qualification session?

reverify.command: With a project open in Logic, call logic_project.new and read the envelope.
reverify.expected: State C `unsupported_state`, with a hint naming how many windows are open and stating that nothing was attempted.

method: Driven once through the release binary with the operator's project open, and the window list read immediately afterwards to confirm nothing had been created.

observations.source: the qualification sweep's own classification of its deferrals, same day
observations.note: the count this record's conclusion refers to

observations.hint: project.new requires Logic to have no open document; 3 window(s) are open. With a document already open a newly created project cannot be told apart from the windows already on screen, so nothing was attempted.
observations.note: the refusal is fail-closed and precise: it names the count it saw and says no attempt was made

conclusion: The destructive half of the qualification program cannot be run from a session that has the operator's project open, and the reason is a deliberate product contract rather than a gap. `project.new` refuses while any document is open, because a newly created project could not be told apart from the windows already on screen — so it will not create one it cannot then identify. That is the right refusal, and it settles the SHAPE of Phase C-live: it needs Logic running with no open document, which means a dedicated qualification session rather than a phase bolted onto the same sweep that qualifies the read-only and reversible operations. Anything that tries to create its disposable fixture mid-sweep will meet this refusal, and the 32 destructive operations stay deferred until the run topology accounts for it.
limits: One call on one host. Whether `project.new` succeeds on a Logic with no open document was NOT tested here — that would have required closing the operator's project, and the refusal already answers the question that was asked.
This says nothing about the other lifecycle operations. `project.close`, `project.save_as` and `project.quit` have their own preconditions and none of them were driven.
It does not establish that a dedicated session is SUFFICIENT, only that the current topology is insufficient. The New Project chooser's own accessibility surface is a separate known wall.
